name: Salzer Electronics
tagline: T&D/electrification tailwind, but margin and guidance-credibility concerns cap conviction at Medium
verdict_headline: Genuine multi-segment T&D/RDSS tailwind undercut by commodity-driven margin misses and a weak execution track record
verdict_reasoning: Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation weak) permits 100x-in-10-years, but conviction set separately
FY26 revenue +24% YoY to Rs1,758cr (5yr CAGR 23%) confirms real demand tailwind across switchgear/wires&cables/exports
But EBITDA margin guidance cut twice in 2026 (10% -> 9-9.5% -> 8-8.5%) and Q1 FY27 PAT fell 52% YoY on copper/silver/aluminium cost inflation with delayed pass-through
Smart meter plant (~Rs25cr invested, 4M-unit capacity) generated only ~Rs25-26cr FY26 revenue -- a 2+ year underutilised asset with guidance 'cut repeatedly and missed' per independent forensics

ROCE ~11.2% (declining per multi-year forensic read) and working-capital-funded debt (short-term borrowings Rs503cr FY26) growing faster than EBITDA -- Coffee-Can track-record test fails on the capital-efficiency leg despite strong revenue growth
Saudi plant and BBMP/Effilume ramp are real but small, dated optionality (commissioning already slipped twice) layered on a base business still proving it can hold margin
business_overview: Coimbatore-based industrial switchgear, wires & cables and building-electrical manufacturer riding India's T&D/electrification capex cycle, diversifying into RDSS smart meters, EV charging (Ultrafast Chargers, 30% stake), municipal energy-management (Effilume SPV, BBMP smart street-lighting, 41.91% stake) and a new Saudi Arabia switchgear plant. FY26 revenue mix: Industrial Switchgear 56% (+20% YoY), Wire & Cable 38.9% (+30% YoY, fastest-growing), Building Electrical ~6% (+16-48% YoY depending on quarter). Exports ~18.6% of revenue, targeting 25%.
fundamentals_narrative: Top-line momentum is real and broad-based: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY to Rs1,758cr on a 23% 5-year CAGR, with wires & cables (+30%) and exports (+rising toward 25% of sales) leading. But profitability has been repeatedly undercut by raw-material (copper/silver/aluminium) cost inflation that outran the company's pass-through mechanism: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 8.36% from 9.44%, and Q1 FY27 collapsed further to ~6%, driving a 52% YoY PAT decline and a second EBITDA-margin guidance cut within the year (10% -> 9-9.5% -> 8-8.5%). Management is responding with price hikes (15% in Feb 2026, 7-10% more planned) and a target to shorten the cost pass-through cycle from a quarter to under two months, but has not yet proven it can hold margin through a commodity cycle. ROCE of 11.2% is unexceptional for a 23%-CAGR business and, per independent forensic reads, has been declining even without major new capex -- working capital (153 days, ~30% of revenue, vs a 25% target) and short-term borrowings (Rs503cr in FY26) are growing faster than EBITDA. The smart-meter plant (~Rs25cr capex, 4M-unit capacity) remains a 2+ year underutilised asset generating only ~Rs25-26cr of FY26 revenue after the Tamil Nadu tender was cancelled. Saudi Arabia plant commissioning has slipped from June to Sep-Oct 2026 and the BBMP/Effilume municipal energy contract is ramping but small relative to the base business. Net: a real demand tailwind sitting on top of a company that has not yet demonstrated pricing power or disciplined capital allocation.

bull_case: Structural, multi-year India T&D/electrification capex cycle plus RDSS smart-meter rollout and export growth (18.6% -> 25% target) give genuine revenue runway independent of any single order
Wires & cables, the fastest-growing segment (+30% FY26), is mix-shifting the business toward higher-margin, higher-multiple peers (Polycab, KEI-type positioning)

Price hikes (15% Feb 2026 + 7-10% more planned) and a shorter cost pass-through cycle, if they stick, could restore EBITDA margin toward the 8.5-9.5% guided range and re-rate a currently depressed earnings base
Saudi plant, BBMP/Effilume municipal energy contract and EV-charging stake are small today but are genuine new-vertical optionality not yet reflected in consensus-free, reverse-P/E-implied numbers
bear_case: Management has cut EBITDA margin guidance twice in 2026 (10% -> 9-9.5% -> 8-8.5%) and the smart-meter business guidance has been 'cut repeatedly and missed' per independent forensic coverage -- a credibility problem, not a one-off

ROCE (11.2%, declining) and working-capital-funded debt growth (short-term borrowings Rs503cr FY26, WC at 153 days / 30% of revenue) show capital efficiency deteriorating even without major new capex -- the Coffee-Can persistence test (revenue growth + ROCE both clearing bars) fails

No clear structural moat: the company is a price-taker on commodity inputs with a multi-quarter pass-through lag, competing in a crowded switchgear/wires space against larger, better-capitalised peers
Smart-meter plant (~Rs25cr invested) sits 2+ years into a cycle at a fraction of its 4M-unit capacity with no near-term tender visibility; Saudi plant commissioning has already slipped twice
At 21.2x trailing P/E on a currently-depressed and still-compressing earnings base, the stock is not pricing in execution risk -- a further margin miss has real downside

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium. Revenue tailwind is confirmed and broad-based, but two guidance cuts in one year, a 2+ year underutilised smart-meter asset, declining ROCE and working-capital-funded debt growth are real execution and capital-efficiency concerns that the Light-entry pass hadn't yet surfaced -- conviction moves down one notch pending a margin-recovery print.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Revenue YoY: FY25 +21.6%, FY26 +24.0%, Q1 FY27 +13% (Rs441cr -> Rs486-498cr) -- growth rate decelerating even as cost inflation compresses margin faster than revenue is growing

four_box.note: T&D/electrification capex cycle + RDSS smart-meter rollout + export growth = genuine structural tailwind (yes) across multiple segments, confirmed by 23% 5yr revenue CAGR = tam yes. But no pricing power (two EBITDA margin guidance cuts in 2026, Q1 FY27 PAT -52% on commodity costs) = moat weak; 21.2x trailing P/E on a currently-depressed, still-compressing earnings base = valuation weak. Score 3.0 supports 100x-in-10-years per the decision table, but conviction is set separately and capped given the margin/management-credibility concerns.

track_record.note: FY24-FY26: revenue growth cleared 10% in every year (FY25 +21.6%, FY26 +24.0%), but ROCE (currently 11.2%, independently flagged as declining) has not cleared the 15% bar in any of these years despite strong top-line growth -- the Coffee-Can persistence test fails on the capital-efficiency leg.

working_capital.note: Cash conversion cycle improved to 153 days in FY26 from 170 days in FY25, but still consumes ~30% of revenue vs the company's own 25% target; individual inventory/receivable/payable day components and a sector-peer comparison were not cleanly sourced this pass.
